claims.text: The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy forms a coherent nanoscale BCC precipitate structure under the stated service conditions.
The coherent nanoscale BCC precipitate structure governs the plastic strain of WTaTiVZr.
The coherent nanoscale BCC precipitate structure governs the toughness of WTaTiVZr.
The BCC precipitate structure increases resistance to dislocation glide.
The BCC precipitate structure increases resistance to grain-boundary sliding.
Increased resistance to dislocation glide and grain-boundary sliding improves plastic strain relative to pure tungsten.
Increased resistance to dislocation glide and grain-boundary sliding improves toughness relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit a 20% increase in plastic strain relative to pure tungsten under the same conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit a 30% increase in toughness relative to pure tungsten under the same conditions.
In situ neutron diffraction and post-mortem TEM can measure the stated plastic-strain and toughness improvements.
The proposed mechanism is valid from 500°C to 1000°C.
The proposed mechanism is valid up to a neutron fluence of 10^20 neutrons/m².
The tested WTaTiVZr material is recrystallized and fully dense.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 20% and 30% improvements, but the falsification rule requires only a statistically significant improvement of any magnitude. Thus, substantially smaller improvements could contradict the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
The test conditions specify an ion flux, whereas the validity boundary is expressed as neutron fluence; no neutron-irradiation exposure or duration is specified to connect these regimes.
